title: SpaceX Stock Surges as Morgan Stanley Says Stock ‘Cheap and Getting Cheaper’
source_used: Investopedia text (by Aaron Rennie) on its AOL.ca copy; Yahoo Finance's report of the same Morgan Stanley note for the detail; Chosunbiz for the close and a second cause. Investopedia original not opened (HTTP 402).
key_facts: SpaceX (officially Space Exploration Technologies, SPCX) shares jumped about 5.5% on Monday 5 Oct 2026, to levels not seen since July, after Morgan Stanley analysts wrote that, adjusted for growth, the company is 'one of the cheaper ways' to play the space and intelligence economy.
Morgan Stanley kept its overweight rating and $300 price target while shares traded above $167; Visible Alpha's mean target is $281.
Shares opened at $150 in the June debut, traded around $105 before a recent surge and finished last week around $159.
Yahoo Finance (note by analyst Adam Jonas): SpaceX trades at about 30 times 2028 EV/EBIT against about 16 times for mega-cap AI enablers, but about 40% below their growth-adjusted median.
Jonas said investor interest has been limited ('not a single hand went up' among 40 clients asked who owns it) and estimated the market assigns about $32 per share to AI.
Risks listed: slower Starship reusability progress, lower enterprise AI monetisation, higher compute costs per watt, longer time-to-power, additional funding needs and regulatory delays.
Chosunbiz: SpaceX closed up 7.63% and Elon Musk's remarks about talks with TSMC on chip production facilities also helped lift the stock.
quote_evidence: SpaceX shares rose Monday after Morgan Stanley said the stock was “cheap and getting cheaper” relative to its growth prospects.
Morgan Stanley maintained an overweight rating and $300 price target as shares traded above $167.

Morgan Stanley identified risks including slower progress on Starship reusability, lower enterprise AI monetisation, higher compute costs per watt, longer time-to-power requirements, additional funding needs and regulatory delays.
why_it_matters_hint: A large bank's analysts call the new AI-and-space company cheap for its growth, and the shares jumped, but it is one opinion.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 (note published a day earlier per Investopedia)
notes: Investopedia page blocked (HTTP 402); text read on AOL.ca copy. Investopedia says the note came a day before Monday's rise; Chosunbiz gives a second cause (Musk's TSMC remarks) and a 7.63% close. Analyst opinion, not company news.
